messages:
sara_cs: Heads up — two customers reported a retrieval/reranking quality regression after today's reranker rollout. They describe worse grounding, missing citations, and notably lower recall on long-tail queries. Examples below, urgent triage requested.

Customer excerpt (quoted by CS): "Before the rollout the top 3 results included exact KB article links. After: top results are generic summaries with no citations. Sample query: 'refund policy for subscription pause' Request ID: req_0a1b2c3d Model: open-reranker-v2 Index: kb-main-v3 Timestamp: 1799201234"

sara_cs: Quick repro steps we ran: 1) GET /search?q=<query>&index=kb-main-v3 2) POST /rerank {model:open-reranker-v2, docs:top50} 3) compare top-k docs. On our sample set recall dropped ~0.82 -> 0.46 after the rollout.

james_eng: @sara_cs thanks — what's the deploy id/commit and canary percent? Need request IDs, any logs we can grab to reproduce.

deploy-bot: Deployed open-reranker-v2 at 1799201200 by @mei_ml. Canary: 35% traffic. Commit: a1b2c3d4. Config change: default `fusion_lambda` changed from `0.6` -> `0.35`.

mei_ml: Confirmed — my change lowered fusion_lambda to reduce latency for long queries. I didn't expect recall regression to be this large on long-tail. I reproduced locally on the head dataset and saw significant drop in exact-match recall. Opening hotfix PR now.

raj_oncall: We should be able to rollback canary to 0% immediately to stop further exposure. @deploy-bot can you set canary=0 and route traffic back to reranker-v1? Also capture traces/req ids for the 35% window.

deploy-bot: Rolling canary back to 0%... done. Traffic routed to reranker-v1 for all new requests. Note: cached sessions may continue to hit v2 for up to 60s.

tom_support: I've messaged the impacted customers to acknowledge the regression and that we've temporarily reverted the rollout. Asked them for any additional repro examples and full request payloads. :pray:

james_eng: Please dump reranker scoring distributions for the affected window (1799201200-1799203600). Quick glance at logs shows mean `reranker_score` dropped from ~0.72 -> ~0.44. Sample log snippet: `{"req_id":"req_0a1b2c3d","scores":[0.84,0.62,0.18],"fusion_lambda":0.35}`

mei_ml: Pushed PR to restore `fusion_lambda=0.6` and to add an AB-test gate + auto-eval. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/p/reranker/merge/1254. Running unit + ranking-eval suites. If green, will promote and re-run a constrained canary with long-tail evals.

raj_oncall: Short-term mitigation suggestion: enable a fallback that triggers when top reranker score < 0.3 to use BM25-only ranking and surface citation hints. Can that be toggled live?

james_eng: Yes — there's a feature flag `reranker_fallback_threshold`. Toggling it now.

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: `reranker_fallback_threshold=0.3` across prod.

mei_ml: Running full eval on our long-tail benchmark now. Quick numbers: with `fusion_lambda=0.6` recall ~0.78, with 0.35 recall ~0.47. Latency delta was small (p95 +30ms) so the recall hit is not worth it. Investigating why the fusion weighting had such non-linear impact on certain queries.

tom_support: Notified customers that we've rolled back to previous config and are running a full investigation. Will follow up tomorrow with ETA. Thanks everyone.

james_eng: Next steps / owners: 1) RCA — why did lambda change get merged/deployed without long-tail perf QA (@mei_ml) 2) Ops safeguards — auto-eval + rollout gates for ranking models (@james_eng) 3) Customer comms and case follow-up (@sara_cs). Also create a postmortem after RCA.

production-monitor: Incident created: INC-2026-3421. Severity: P2. Linked items: deploy logs (a1b2c3d4), PR-1254, feature-flag change.

sara_cs: Thanks team. I'll collect the customer repro payloads and escalate priority if they provide more failing examples. Keep updates in this thread and I'll consolidate for CS follow-up.
